# Bundled third-party sources

## OpenRGB 1.1 — `third_party/openrgb/`

| | |
|---|---|
| Project | OpenRGB — Open source RGB lighting control |
| Upstream | https://gitlab.com/CalcProgrammer1/OpenRGB (mirror: https://github.com/CalcProgrammer1/OpenRGB) |
| Version | 1.1: tag `release_1.1` (2026-10-16) |
| Commit | `8e16de27858cf2be6af54a33ce003df74cb9fd3e` (2026-10-16), also in `openrgb.commit` |
| Why 1.1 | The current stable release: everything added to master since 1.0 (MSI B650M/B850M ARGB, real ARGB header sizes on MSI 761-byte boards, ASUS Aura USB 500-LED Direct mode, ENE DIMM_LED-0103 RAM, Corsair Lighting Node / Hydro Platinum lock-up fixes, many GPUs…), plus a deadlock fix for ENE SMBus RAM and motherboards, mode and LED updates kept in order, hot-plug and Sinowealth fixes, Cooler Master ARGB Gen2 A1 V2, MSI RTX 3070 Gaming Trio Plus, Kreo Swarm (wired) |
| Licence | GPL-2.0-or-later (see `openrgb/LICENSE`) |
| Modifications | Two small patches, in `patches/` and already applied to the tree. `0001`: each controller's device thread waits for its updates instead of checking for them every millisecond (OpenRGB used about 10 % of a core while idle with six controllers; now next to nothing). `0002`: builds with MinGW-w64 (one line in hueplusplus, Windows only). Everything else is the unmodified upstream commit (without `.git`). |

TuxRGB does not link OpenRGB: it runs the `openrgb` binary as a
separate, private process (`openrgb --server --server-host 127.0.0.1
--server-port 6743 --noautoconnect --config ~/.config/tuxrgb/openrgb`) and
talks to it over the OpenRGB SDK protocol (v6, unchanged in master). This directory is shipped so
that every TuxRGB package that contains an OpenRGB binary also provides its
complete corresponding source code, as required by the GPL.

### Building it by hand

```sh
sudo apt install qt6-base-dev qt6-l10n-tools libhidapi-dev libusb-1.0-0-dev libmbedtls-dev   # Debian/Ubuntu
sudo dnf install qt6-qtbase-devel qt6-linguist hidapi-devel libusb1-devel mbedtls-devel       # Fedora
mkdir build-openrgb && cd build-openrgb
qmake6 ../third_party/openrgb/OpenRGB.pro CONFIG+=release
make -j"$(nproc)"
./openrgb --version
```

`packaging/appimage/build-appimage.sh` does exactly this (or reuses a binary
given through `OPENRGB_BIN=`), and the Flatpak manifest builds the same tree.

### Windows build (since TuxRGB 3.6)

The Windows installer carries OpenRGB built from this same tree, so it gets
the same patches as the AppImage. `scripts/windows/build-openrgb-windows.sh`
cross-compiles everything from Linux with MinGW-w64 (posix threads):

* Qt 5.15.16 LTS (qtbase: Core, Gui, Widgets) from https://github.com/qt/qtbase,
  unmodified;
* Mbed TLS 3.2.1 (the version OpenRGB ships for Windows) from
  https://github.com/Mbed-TLS/mbedtls, unmodified;
* OpenRGB, with `OpenRGB.pro` adjusted on the qmake command line only: no
  MSVC `/utf-8` flag, the architecture given (`QMAKE_TARGET.arch=x86_64`,
  read from Visual Studio otherwise), Mbed TLS and libusb linked from the
  MinGW builds, a `comsupp.cpp` standing in for MSVC's `comsupp.lib`, and
  `<Windows.h>`-style header names mapped to MinGW's lower-case headers.

libusb 1.0.27, hidapi (hotplug) and PawnIOLib are the prebuilt DLLs OpenRGB
ships in `openrgb/dependencies` (plain C interfaces). Like the official
OpenRGB build, the hidapi DLL needs the Visual C++ runtime
(`vcruntime140.dll`), present on most Windows installations.

```sh
sudo apt install g++-mingw-w64-x86-64-posix cmake ninja-build qt6-l10n-tools
scripts/windows/build-openrgb-windows.sh      # about 1 h the first time (Qt), then minutes
```

The result goes to `build/openrgb-windows/`, which
`scripts/windows/build-windows.sh` puts in the installer.

### Refreshing the tree

`third_party/fetch-openrgb.sh [commit|branch|tag]` replaces
`third_party/openrgb/` with a fresh copy (default: the pinned commit;
`master` for the very latest devices). Then rebuild the AppImage: the build
script regenerates `data/udev/60-openrgb.rules` from the new binary (the
rules are compiled into TuxRGB so the password dialog opens instantly).
Check that the helper still accepts every generated rule:

```sh
cargo test -p tuxrgb-helper
```

## Material Symbols Rounded — `crates/tuxrgb/assets/fonts/`

Subset (≈100 glyphs) of Google's Material Symbols Rounded, Apache-2.0,
generated by `scripts/gen-icon-font.py` (instructions inside the script).
